transcript.text: my oven fan keeps going after ive turned the oven off, been about 20 mins now. is it broken??

Probably not broken. Most ovens have a separate cooling fan (a quiet whirring, usually from the top or behind the controls) that keeps running after you switch off, to protect the controls and the kitchen units from the heat. It carries on until the inside has cooled, and 10–30 minutes is quite typical, longer after a long or very hot cook or a grill session. A few simple checks will tell you whether yours is behaving normally: 1. Let it run and note when it stops. If it switches itself off within roughly 30–45 minutes, that's normal overrun and nothing needs doing.
2. Leave the door closed while it cools. Opening it doesn't help much, and the fan is simply waiting for the temperature to drop.
3. Listen to where the sound comes from. A soft whirr near the top or controls is the cooling fan, which is expected. If you can see the fan at the back of the oven cavity spinning through the glass after switch-off, that's less usual and worth mentioning.
4. Make sure the vents above the door or around the controls aren't blocked by tea towels or anything leaning against them. Poor airflow makes it cool more slowly, so the fan runs longer. It becomes a fault if the fan never stops even when the oven is completely cold (for example, it's still running an hour or two later or the next morning). That usually points to the cooling-fan thermostat or its control sticking on. It's not dangerous in the short term, but it does need an engineer to sort out. Let me know whether it stops on its own once the oven has cooled.

ok it does stop by itself eventually, usually after about 20-30 mins, it ran longer today after a long roast. warm air is coming out of the slot above the door and no weird smells or noises. so is that normal?

Yes, that's normal. A fan that stops on its own after 20–30 minutes, runs a bit longer after a long roast, and pushes warm air out of the slot above the door is the cooling fan doing its job. It clears the heat away from the controls and your kitchen units, and it's set to switch off once the oven has cooled enough. A long roast heats the oven body more, so it takes longer to cool. No odd smells or noises is a good sign too. There's nothing you need to do. Just keep that slot above the door clear so the air can get out, and don't hang tea towels over the door while it's cooling. 1. That points to the cooling-fan thermostat or control sticking on.
2. The fan stops running during or after cooking, and the knobs, fascia or the cupboards around the oven get hotter than usual. If that happens, stop using the oven until it's repaired, because the controls can overheat.
3. The oven cuts out once it's hot and then works again after it has cooled down.
4. You hear a new grinding, rattling or scraping, or smell burning. Otherwise, you can carry on using it as normal.

candidates: Normal cooling fan overrun after use (high)
Cooling fan thermostat/control stuck on (fan never stops even when cold) (low)
Cooling fan running but airflow restricted so the oven cools slowly (low)
